content:
Alex K: heads up — found a weird billing gap during a local repro. streaming session resumed after a network hiccup and the dashboard shows provisional tokens + final tokens both counted for ~2s window.
Priya S: ugh. repro steps?
Alex K: start a stream with a tool invocation (internal-search), kill connection, reconnect with resume_token. server responds with a partial chunk + replayed tokens. dashboard shows both provisional and final lines.
Sam T: is this the heartbeat/resume race we chatted about last week?
Alex K: similar but different: the provisional ledger entry never got marked reconciled because the handoff path used a different session id. looks like routing swapped to a failover host that didn't have the provisional marker.
Jordan L: can you paste logs?
Alex K: log snippet — notice resume_id mismatch and duplicate charge markers:

```
[2026-02-12T18:22:43Z] session_start id=abc123 host=ip-10-0-1-7
[2026-02-12T18:22:53Z] chunk_sent tokens=48 offset=0 provisional=true ledger_tx=tx789
[2026-02-12T18:22:55Z] conn_lost session_id=abc123
[2026-02-12T18:22:56Z] conn_reconnect new_host=ip-10-0-2-4 resume_id=resume-xyz session_id=abc123
[2026-02-12T18:22:57Z] chunk_resend tokens=48 offset=0 provisional=false ledger_tx=tx790
```

Maria G: so tx789 (provisional) and tx790 (final) both show up in telemetry, but reconciler only looks for ledger_tx on the original host to flip provisional->confirmed. failover path creates a new ledger entry instead.
Priya S: suggestion: include a resume_token header that we use as the canonical id for ledger reconciliation, not host-local session_id. then reconciler can match across hosts.
Sam T: that works but we'd need to propagate resume_token everywhere we write provisional rows. Also need to ensure resume_token is unique and unguessable (signed).
Jordan L: any UX impact? Console currently shows provisional units as "tentative" and final as "billed". Users see a spike then a single final line most times. In this case they see both and think we double-billed.
Maria G: can we change the console to de-dupe provisional+final by resume_token if both appear in the same window? quick fix while infra change rolls out.
Alex K: yep, add a client-side de-dupe rule in billing UI: if two ledger rows share resume_token (or session_start_id) and timestamps within 10s, show as one with a note.
Priya S: ops concern: reconciler needs idempotency and backwards compat. Some older clients won't send resume_token yet. we should fallback to session_id matching and host mapping.
Sam T: internal API debate: should resume_token be injected by the router (edge) or by the serving runtime? If router signs it we avoid trusting client. But router doesn't know KV cache keys for partials.
Jordan L: prefer router-signed resume_token: router already does affinity and has the failover metadata. sign as HMAC over (session_id, generation, timestamp). runtime verifies and uses value as canonical_resume_id.
Maria G: ops-bot: what's the rollout plan for adding resume_token to provisional writes?
ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-02-15 02:00 UTC to 3 hosts in us-west-2; monitoring: billing-ledger-rate, provisional-to-final-lag, dashboard-de-dupe-rate.
Alex K: timeline seems fine. action items: 1) infra: router add signed resume_token header (Sam) 2) runtime: persist resume_token on provisional writes + reconciler match on resume_token (Priya) 3) console: de-dupe UI by resume_token and show "merged provisional" hint (Jordan) 4) telemetry: add metric provisional_duplicates_per_min (Maria)
Priya S: question on reconciler: do we mark provisional rows as tombstones or update them to confirmed? current job rewrites row status=true. with resume_token matching across hosts we'll have two rows — prefer update + tombstone the other to keep audit.
Sam T: prefer: create a canonical row and emit a tombstone event for duplicates. keeps audit trail and makes final aggregation easier. but that requires tombstone-aware aggregations.
Jordan L: console aggregation already treats tombstone as 'merged' if flagged. we'll wire it up.
Maria G: telemetry — to prove we fixed it we should capture a sample id of affected requests and include that in the alert (ex: sample_resume_ids).
Alex K: UX faux pas: avoid changing billing language that scares customers. prefer 'temporary duplicate display resolved' copy.
Priya S: quick patch idea for older clients: if resume_token missing, reconciler uses (session_id, first_chunk_checksum) fingerprint to match duplicates. less ideal but helps migration.
Sam T: implementation note: make resume_token TTL at least 1 minute longer than max resume window (currently 120s) to allow reconciler to find it.
Jordan L: tests: e2e simulate failover, assert only one billed row in UI after reconciler run. Also load test reconciler with 10k provisional rows/min.
Maria G: I'll add dashboards: "provisional dup ratio", "reconcile-latency P95", and a small chart on affected customers.
Alex K: ok I'm going to post a short RFC doc in #eng-runtime with the proposed header and reconciler changes. will link here.
Priya S: LGTM. thanks for catching this. :pray:
Sam T: ping me if you want pairing on the router signing bits.
ops-bot: deploy-canary started for us-west-2 hosts (canary-id=canary-20260215-01)
Alex K: noted — will watch telemetry.
Maria G: can we also add a console hint for internal support: if a customer pings about duplicate rows, we can filter by resume_token and show 'merged by reconciler' in the internal view. easier triage.
Jordan L: will add that support column.
Alex K: thanks all — reopening if anything odd shows in the canary.
